newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle set new highs on strong cash ideas.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle set new highs on strong cash ideas.

text.p: Expectations for further strength in cash cattle prices and buy stops boosted most months of CME live cattle futures to new contract highs before easing slightly at the close on profit taking, traders said.
Only June and August live cattle failed to post new highs with April setting a new high of 69.950 cents a lb before futures ended 0.475 to 0.225 up with April up most at 69.725.
The strong tone in cash cattle and beef prices and spillover from sharply higher to limit up from pork pits combined to boost futures to new highs, traders said.
General buying touched off buy stops early in the session but gains were curbed by profit taking and scale up resistance from the large premium that futures already hold to cash.
Cash cattle last traded in volume at $66 per cwt versus the April live cattle futures close at 69.725 cents a lb.
Beef values surged late Friday and were up again Monday and expectations were for packers to pay $67 per cwt for cash cattle in the Plains some time this week, sources said.

"The cattle (futures) market is advancing on the expectation that packers by midweek will be paying $1 to $2 (per cwt) higher for live cash cattle," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.
Friday's USDA Cold Storage Report was also considered bullish to cattle as it showed frozen beef stocks well under year-ago levels, sources said.
The USDA reported beef stocks as of February 1 at 290.3 million lbs versus 367.9 million lbs last year.

Rand Financials, R.J. O'Brien and ABN Chicago Corp notably bought April while Lind-Waldock bought June. Shatkin Arbor actively sold April at the high with Cargill Investor Services selling June late. In options, there was renewed short covering by commission houses, buying April 68 and 70 calls. One commission house sold 70 calls, pit sources said.

Feeder cattle futures followed the lead of live cattle and pork pits with buy stops touched off on the advance. Adding to support was a higher CME feeder cattle index and lower corn futures, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.10 at $68.98 per cwt.
ABN Chicogo Corp was a notable buyer early while Refco and bought late and E.D.& F. Man spread long May/short March, pit sources said.
